subject: Lighting and power for productive work
hook: From bare box room to working office: where power fits in.
ig:
From bare box room to working office: here's where power and light fit into every stage, not just the last one.

A fresh start in January often means finally giving the spare room a job. This is a typical layout of how we take one from empty to usable:

Survey: sockets, switches, radiators and windows go on the drawing first.
Design: the screen sits side-on to the window and grommets go where your devices will be.
Workshop: grommet holes and cut-outs are drilled before assembly in Hanley.
Installation: our own team fits it with sockets still reachable.
Handover: a clear worktop, cables out of sight, a spot for a task lamp.

The images here are concept images showing the principle. For genuine finished work, our showcase is the place to look.

Save this if you're planning a fitted home office, and use the link in bio to see real SUPERIO projects.
fb:
New year, new use for the spare room? Here's how a fitted home office typically comes together, with power and lighting thought about at every stage.

We start by marking every socket and switch at the survey, design the desk so the screen avoids window glare, drill the cable grommets in our workshop before anything is assembled, then fit it so you can still reach your plugs.

These are concept images to show the steps. If you'd like to see real finished SUPERIO furniture, take a look at our showcase.

on_asset: F1: Survey — We measure the room and mark every socket, switch, radiator and window on the drawing, so nothing gets boxed in by mistake. | F2: Design — The desk is positioned side-on to the window, with grommets placed where the screen and laptop will sit. | F3: Workshop — Panels are cut, edged and drilled for grommets and cut-outs before the carcass is assembled and checked. | F4: Installation — Our team fits the desk with sockets still reachable and a single hidden route for cables to the wall. | F5: Handover — A clear worktop, a tray holding the adaptors, and room for a task lamp on the side you need it. | Concept image
